name: bluewater-19-who-killed-this-business
lines: A business was found dead on a Tuesday.
Twelve years old. One van. Four hundred happy customers.
No break in. No fire. No lawsuit. It just, stopped.
Five suspects were in the room. One of them did it.
And it's the one nobody ever suspects.
The victim. A plumbing company. Made up, like everyone in this story. The cause of death is real.
The owner, Hank, found it. He opened the calendar on a Tuesday morning, and there was nothing on it.
Nothing Wednesday. Nothing all month.
Let's question the suspects.
Suspect one. The website.
Last updated in twenty sixteen. Still advertising a holiday special. For a holiday in twenty sixteen.
Where were you the night the business died? Loading, says the website. I'm still loading.
Guilty of being embarrassing. But customers were still finding it. It didn't do this.
Suspect two. The voicemail.
Full. Obviously. But here's the thing.
Hank answers his phone. Every time. The voicemail never got the chance to hurt anybody.
Released without charge.
Suspect three. The nephew.
He ran the Instagram. Three posts. One is a sunset. One is a sandwich. One says, coming soon.
Did you kill the business? I don't even know the password anymore.
He's innocent. Useless. But innocent.
Suspect four. The price.
Everybody's favorite suspect. Too high. Had to be.
Except the detective checked. Hank's customers never complained about the price. Not once in twelve years.
The price has an alibi.
Suspect five.
The best friend. Word of mouth.
Everybody loves this guy. He brought Hank every customer he ever had.
For twelve years, Hank never spent a dollar on marketing. Didn't need to. His buddy handled it.
The detective almost let him go.
Then she looked at where the customers actually came from.
The evidence.
Four hundred customers. And nearly all of them traced back to three people.
A realtor. A property manager. And a retired guy named Lou, who told the whole street.
Three people. That was the entire marketing department.
Two years ago, the realtor moved away.
Last spring, the property manager's company was sold. New owner. New plumber.
And in January, Lou's knee gave out. He stopped walking the street.
Nobody attacked this business. Its three best friends just, quietly, left the room.
Word of mouth didn't kill it on purpose.
It did something worse. It made Hank feel safe.
So here's the detective's report.
Word of mouth is the best customer you'll ever get. It is a terrible only plan.
Because you don't control it. You can't turn it up. And it never warns you before it leaves.
Three things would have saved this business.
One. A second way in. A listing people can actually find, with real photos, and reviews from this year.
Two. Ask every customer for a review. That turns one friend's opinion into something a stranger can read.
Three. Know your sources. If three people send you everything, you don't have a business. You have three friends.
Count yours tonight. It takes ten minutes.
The honest part. None of this pays off next week.
And nobody can promise how many calls a listing brings.
But a business with one way in is one retirement party away from an empty calendar.
Hank's story is made up. So he gets a second ending.
He claims the listing. He texts forty old customers. Twelve leave a review.
In the spring, a stranger calls. She says, I found you online.
Hank almost drops the phone. That had never happened before.
Word of mouth is still his best friend. It's just not his only one.
Case closed.
If you want more than one way in, that's what we build. Bluewater Co dot C A.
